newsitem.title: UK: Origins mixed in routine sugar freight business.
newsitem.headline: Origins mixed in routine sugar freight business.

text.p: Activity was routine on the sugar freight market on Thursday with north African and Middle East countries providing most of the demand but the origins were mixed, shipbrokers said.
Iranian shippers IRISL quoted for 14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from the European Union, excluding Britain, to Iran for Jaunary dates.
E D & F Man fixed two of its recent orders and was open with further inquiry.

It covered 25,000 tonnes in bulk from Puerto Quetzal to Morocco, with Egyptian Med and Black Sea options, for 1/10 December and further 12/12,250 tonnes from Maputo to Portugal for early December. Details of the rates are as yet unknown.
Man was also open for 5/6,000 tonnes in bags from Eemshaven to the Turkish Med for prompt onwards and 4,500 tonnes from Gdynia/Gdansk to Mersin.
Shipbrokers cited an unnamed Russian account order for 10,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Rio de Janeiro to the Egyptian Med for 1/15 December.
Korean operators Halla fixed 38,000 tonnes for timecharter with Recife delivery, Iran trip, for November dates at a daily $8,000 plus $200,000 bonus, they said.
